question: One question about your answer. The topic's outcome names two things: whether meaningful new HBM capacity comes online, and whether record-high prices persist. The request says to return no_ladder when "the topic has no main figure or event, naming none, or naming several with none of them the main one", and never to combine two things. You wrote a judged question. Which sentences of the request led you to write one here rather than return no_ladder? Quote each, and say which weighed most. Then say what, in the request, would have made you decline. Answer in at most 180 words.
reply:
The sentence that led me to write a judged question was: “A topic's wording may ask about more than one thing. Judge the one the topic's outcome names as what is tracked.” I treated “the state of HBM supply and pricing” as one tracked outcome.

But I should have followed: “Never fold two things into one ladder.” The topic’s outcome names both new capacity and record-high prices, without identifying either as the main one. The most relevant no-ladder rule is: “the topic has no main figure or event, naming none, or naming several with none of them the main one.” That rule should have weighed most.

I should therefore have returned no_ladder, rather than combining capacity and prices into one set of states. I would decline whenever the topic names multiple figures or events and neither is clearly the main tracked outcome; I would also decline if no main figure or event is named.
